Suppose the recurrence is nondegenerate: no complex root of its characteristic polynomial…
nodes.title: Few small values of a nondegenerate integer linear recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega(n)$ be the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity. There is a constant $C$ such that for every real $x \ge 10$, the number of integers $1 \le n \le x$ with $\Omega(n) \ge 10 \log\log x$ is at most $C x / (\log x)^2$.
nodes.title: Integers with many prime factors are rare

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma(n)$ be the sum of the positive divisors of $n$ and $\tau(m)$ the number of positive divisors of $m$. There is a constant $C$ such that for every real $x \ge 10$, the number of integers $1 \le n \le x$ with $\tau(\sigma(n)) > \exp(\sqrt{\log x})$ is at most $C x / (\log x)^2$.
nodes.title: Integers whose sum of divisors has many divisors

nodes.summary: Write $p(n)$ for the least prime factor of an integer $n \ge 2$, and set $p(1) = 1$. There is a constant $C$ such that for all real $x$ and $y$ with $2 \le y \le x$, the number of integers $1 \le n \le x$ with $p(n) > y$ is at most $C x / \log y$.
nodes.title: Sieve bound for integers without small prime factors

nodes.title: Euler's function and the sum of divisors along a linear recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be Euler's totient function and $\sigma(n)$ the sum of the positive divisors of $n$. There is a constant $C > 0$ such that $\varphi(n)/n \ge C/\log\log n$ for every integer $n \ge 3$, and there is a constant $C'$ such that $\sigma(n)/n \le C' \log\log n$ for every integer $n \ge 3$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for Euler's function and upper bound for the sum of divisors

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
